title: Prove Excel/PDF export with nonempty rows and current-user scope on isolated SQL
description: Stage-1 genuine database validation gap. Export endpoints passed HTTP acceptance only with zero rows (Excel 6042 bytes, PDF 69137 bytes), so nonempty cell rendering, current-user data scope, numeric sign preservation and formula-injection escaping on real text are unproven. Implement a self-contained fixture with customers and non-deleted sales orders (including text cells with leading formula-like characters and signed amounts) on the dedicated isolated localdb, drive Excel and PDF export through the existing export path (ReportConfigurationExcelExporter / ReportConfigurationPdfExporter) and assert nonempty cell values, current-user scoped rows, numeric sign preservation and injection-escaped text. No production data, arbitrary SQL, secrets/.env changes, permission expansion or schema change; no SeedData*.cs / SchemaUpgrader.cs edits.
acceptance_criteria: A self-contained fixture seeds activated customers and non-deleted sales orders (including text values with leading formula-like characters and signed amounts) on the dedicated (localdb)\NEWERP_AutoAcceptance / NEWERP_AUTOTEST-prefixed database with target identity asserted before writes; process-only settings, idempotent, never touching SeedData*.cs or SchemaUpgrader.cs.

Excel export with nonempty rows writes the selected nonempty cell values with numeric sign preserved and text escaped against formula injection; PDF export renders nonempty rows with the same bounded preview pipeline (columns/rows bounded, current-user scope applied, read-only).

Exports reflect the current user's data scope (never the owner's full set when scoped) and never return stale downloads after revocation; run focused SQL tests, safe Release build/test and scheduler self-test/contracts. Do not claim full stage-1 or real-browser acceptance.
implementation_evidence: .ai/logs/report-platform-http-acceptance-20261004T0847.json records export bytes 6042 (xlsx) and 69137 (pdf) for preview rows=0, so nonempty export parity is unproven; src/ERP.Api/Controllers/ReportConfigurationsController.cs Export/ExportPdf (lines ~295-316) and RenderExcel/RenderPdf (lines ~363-405) drive ReportConfigurationExcelExporter/ReportConfigurationPdfExporter with no real-SQL test asserting nonempty cells or scoped exports.
